previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic G-tube and TPN dependence, and a history of upper extremity DVTs was admitted for dark-brown G-tube output concerning for gastrointestinal bleeding. She had been on Lovenox for anticoagulation and had a history of prior GI bleeds. Initial evaluation showed guaiac-positive drainage and stable hemoglobin. An endoscopy revealed mild G-tube-related gastritis with no active bleeding, and a small bowel endoscopy was unremarkable. Blood cultures showed no growth, and a urine culture grew Streptococcus anginosus, which was not treated due to lack of symptoms. She was not on IV antibiotics as her recent Enterococcus avium line infection had been completed. Suicidal ideation expressed in the ED was evaluated and cleared by psychiatry. She remained on home medications including ranitidine, anticoagulation, and pain management with gabapentin and amitriptyline. TPN was held during admission and planned for restart at home. She was discharged home with services, stable and with no active bleeding.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with complicated history of 
mesenteric fibromatosis s/p multiple abdominal surgeries for 
SBO/pain, s/p venting g-tube, on home TPN, with chronic poorly 
controlled abdominal pain directly admitted from GI clinic 
because of abdominal pain and malnutrition.
.
# Pain: On admission she had ___ diffuse abdominal pain not 
helped by PO morphine at home; she was continued on her home 
pain regimen and the chronic pain service was consulted. Per 
their recommendations, on hospital day 3 she was started on a 
Dilaudid PCA, Amitriptyline was increased to 100 mg qhs, and 
Gabapentin was increased to 900 mg tid. The PCA was used for 
roughly 24 hrs and then she was switched back to her oral 
morphine regimen.  Within a few hours after stopping the PCA, 
she developed L thigh swelling and ___ pain (see below). On 
hospital day 5, she was started on Dilaudid 0.5 mg IV q3hrs. Per 
chronic pain recs, on hospital day 7 she was started on a 
Fentanyl patch, which was then discontinued after 24 hrs because 
of her prior history of suicidal ideation on Fentanyl. She was 
then started on Buprenorphine sublingual 4 mg qid, which per 
patient provided no relief. On ___, she was switched to 
methadone 5 mg twice daily.
.
# L thigh swelling - on hospital day 3, she complained of a new, 
tender, 6 x 6 cm round region of induration on her L thigh with 
overlying ecchymoses, distal to her Hickman, with no associated 
erythema or warmth. She also had multiple old cords in this 
region which she attributed to her Lovenox injections. 
Ultrasound showed multiple septated fluid collections with a 
differential including abscess or multiple hematomas. She was 
afebrile. Her Lovenox was held, given her numerous bruises and 
suspicion for an expanding hematoma. Vascular surgery was called 
for concern of trauma to her Hickman and felt it was most 
consistent with a hematoma or abscess. Conservative management 
was recommended with warm compresses. At this point her factor 
Xa level came back > 2x assay (nl range 0.6 - 1), suggesting 
that she was supra-therapeutic on her home dose of 80 mg bid. 
She was restarted on prophylactic Lovenox dosing at 40 mg daily 
given her supratherapeutic levels and that her last documented 
DVT was in ___. The hematoma decreased in size over her 
remaining course, and her pain diminished with alternating hot / 
cold packs and lidocaine patches overnight.
.
# Nutrition: She was initially admitted with concern for 
malnutrition evident by albumin of 2 on outside labs and per 
history of discontinuing her home TPN more than 3 weeks prior 
because of nausea and vomiting. Of note, she continued to have 
nausea and vomiting after discontinuing TPN. Her albumin on 
admission was 3.0. Nutrition was consulted and she was started 
on TPN. Her home TPN company was contacted and worked to 
optimize her home formula. They have reportedly exactly 
replicated the ___ TPN formula for her home use. She was 
discharged with TPN per her home company and was tolerating 
clears PO.
.
# Nausea: She was admitted with baseline nausea (___) and 
treated on her home anti-emetics and dysmotility agents. Her 
nausea improved to 3 / 10.
.
# Pruritis - She had intermittent pruritis without rash or clear 
etiology and was treated on home dose oral Benadryl.
.
# Chronic DVTs - She has a history of line-associated DVTs and 
was therefore continued on her home Lovenox, but then switched 
to prophylactic dosing as discussed above.
.
# Recent GI bleed: She was recently admitted for GI bleed, but 
this issue was not active during the current hospitalization. 
She had no clinical evidence of bleeding. She was treated on 
Ranitidine instead of her home Rabeprazole.
.
# Anemia - She has longstanding anemia which is thought to be 
from malabsorption and poor nutrition. She was treated on her 
home iron supplementation and her Hct was monitored. She had a 
slight decrease to 25 from baseline on the day of discharge, and 
so she was written to have her CBC checked the day after 
discharge with follow up in Dr. ___.
.
# Depression: During this admission, she had intermittent 
depressed mood, pressured speech and occasional insomnia, but 
denied active suicidal or homicidal ideation. She was continued 
on her home psych regimen.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ woman, with history of DVT, secondary to line placement.
On anticoagulation now.  Now presents with left leg swelling.  Assess for DVT
versus infiltrates.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Color and gray-scale sonogram was performed of the left lower
extremity.  The left common femoral, superficial femoral and popliteal veins
are normal in compressibility, augmentation, and Doppler waveforms.  The calf
veins are patent and compressible.  There is no evidence of left lower
extremity DVT.  

Targeted ultrasound was performed at the anterior left thigh.  Large, complex
and septated fluid collections measure 3.6 x 2.8 x 1.3 cm and 5.6 x 2.3 x 3.8
cm.  Both collections demonstrate thick wallS, concerning for abscesses.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis.
2.  At least two complex, septated thick-walled fluid collections in the
anterior left thigh, concerning for abscesses.
